title: Permits and bundle discounts

blocks.text: A rural telecom carrier is choosing which tower and backhaul upgrades to build this year. Two contract terms change what a plan really costs:

items: **Permits.** Some upgrades need a permit, for example to cross the river. Each permit in `permits` maps a name to `(fee, projects)`: the fee is paid **once** if *any* of its projects is funded, however many of them are, and not at all if none is.
**Bundle discounts.** Each `(tower, backhaul, discount)` in `bundles` takes `discount` ($k) off the plan's spend when *both* the tower and its backhaul link are funded.

blocks.text: The plan's spend (project costs, plus permit fees, minus bundle discounts) must not exceed `budget`. The model in `towers.py` has a binary `x[pid]` for each upgrade (1 if funded) and no budget row yet. Write `add_fee_rules(model, x, projects, permits, bundles, budget)` so that the model allows exactly the plans whose real spend fits the budget. Add whatever variables you need.
With $`P`$ the upgrades and $`c_p`$ the cost of upgrade $`p`$ ($k), the model so far is only

Write the rest first: each new variable with its domain, the rows that tie it to the $`x_p`$, and the budget row, each labelled. For each new variable, decide which way the solver would like to move it, and make sure your rows stop it.
The tests fix which upgrades are built and ask the solver whether the model accepts the plan, so any correct formulation passes. About twelve lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Upgrade:
    pid: str
    cost: int        # $k


def add_fee_rules(model: mathopt.Model, x: dict, projects: list[Upgrade],
                  permits: dict[str, tuple[int, list[str]]], bundles: list[tuple[str, str, int]],
                  budget: int) -> None:
    """Costs plus each needed permit's fee, once, minus each complete bundle's discount, within budget."""
    charged = []
    for name, (fee, members) in permits.items():
        paid = model.add_binary_variable(name=f"permit_{name}")
        for i in members:
            model.add_linear_constraint(paid >= x[i], name=f"permit_{name}_{i}")
        charged.append(fee * paid)
    for tower, backhaul, discount in bundles:
        both = model.add_binary_variable(name=f"bundle_{tower}_{backhaul}")
        model.add_linear_constraint(both <= x[tower], name=f"bundle_{tower}_{backhaul}_t")
        model.add_linear_constraint(both <= x[backhaul], name=f"bundle_{tower}_{backhaul}_b")
        charged.append(-discount * both)
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(p.cost * x[p.pid] for p in projects) + sum(charged) <= budget,
                                name="budget")


def build(projects: list[Upgrade], permits: dict[str, tuple[int, list[str]]],
          bundles: list[tuple[str, str, int]], budget: int) -> tuple[mathopt.Model, dict]:
    model = mathopt.Model(name="tower-upgrades")
    x = {p.pid: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"x_{p.pid}") for p in projects}
    add_fee_rules(model, x, projects, permits, bundles, budget)
    model.maximize(sum(x.values()))
    return model, x


if __name__ == "__main__":
    upgrades = [Upgrade("T1", 100), Upgrade("B1", 60), Upgrade("C1", 50)]
    model, x = build(upgrades, {"river": (25, ["C1"])}, [("T1", "B1", 40)], 200)
    print(len(list(model.linear_constraints())), "rows")

cases.says: a plan that fits the budget with its permit fee is allowed, and one whose costs fit but whose fee does not is refused
a bundle that fits the budget only after its discount is allowed, and a plan over budget even after it is refused
two projects under one permit pay its fee once
a plan with no project under a permit pays no permit fee
a plan with only one member of a bundle gets no discount

origin.section: Pin Only the Side the Model Would Exploit, or Both When Unsure

concepts: a conjunction or disjunction used as a value is a new binary with rows bounding it from above and below
the direction the solver wants to move a logic variable decides which of its rows are essential
